#### Side effects — stack and heap at every step

**What is being answered.** Why a deduplicating shuffle and an idempotency key are interchangeable for an aggregation and not for a charge — by scoring each against every crash point.

`charge(proc, key, amount)` makes the decision **inside the processor**, which matters because that is the only state that survives the pipeline's crash. Step 1 shows the early return leaving `totalCharged` at 6.

Step 2 is the failure mode worth remembering: `keyFor(e, false)` returns a fresh `"send-N"` per attempt, so the processor sees a new key and charges 12. Everything else about the pipeline is correct. And `coverage` scores the two guards at 1 and 3 of 3.

The animation steps through the code, holding each line long enough to read the STACK (call frames and their locals) and the HEAP (allocated arrays and objects) as they are AT THAT MOMENT. Expand any step to study it on its own.

<img src="../diagrams/anim/ch05-effects-memory/ch05-effects-memory.svg" alt="Side effects — stack and heap at every step, 4 steps showing stack and heap" width="980">

<details>
<summary><b>Step 1 of 4</b> — the processor is the only component that can recognise a repeat</summary>

<img src="../diagrams/anim/ch05-effects-memory/frames/step-01.svg" alt="Step 1: the processor is the only component that can recognise a repeat" width="980">

On the second pass `proc.chargedKeys` already contains "order-4", so the function returns before touching `totalCharged`. It stays 6. Note where that decision is made: inside the processor's state, which is the only state that survived the pipeline's crash.

</details>
<details>
<summary><b>Step 2 of 4</b> — a key generated at SEND TIME defeats the whole mechanism</summary>

<img src="../diagrams/anim/ch05-effects-memory/frames/step-02.svg" alt="Step 2: a key generated at SEND TIME defeats the whole mechanism" width="980">

`nextCounter()` returns 2 on the retry, so the key is "send-2" — which the processor has never seen. It charges again and `totalCharged` reaches 12. The pipeline is using an idempotency key correctly in every respect except where the key came from, and nothing detects the difference.

</details>
<details>
<summary><b>Step 3 of 4</b> — dedup covers 1 crash point, and misses the other 2</summary>

<img src="../diagrams/anim/ch05-effects-memory/frames/step-03.svg" alt="Step 3: dedup covers 1 crash point, and misses the other 2" width="980">

`seen` only gains the id when the crash happens BEFORE the shuffle. For the other 2 crash points the record is already past the dedup set — or the set died with the process — so `contains(seen, ORDER.id)` is false on the retry and the charge runs again.

</details>
<details>
<summary><b>Step 4 of 4</b> — so the two guards are NOT interchangeable here</summary>

<img src="../diagrams/anim/ch05-effects-memory/frames/step-04.svg" alt="Step 4: so the two guards are NOT interchangeable here" width="980">

`byDedup` = 1 and `byKey` = 3. In the previous concept these two guards were redundant for an aggregation; here they are not, and the reason is structural: dedup is inside the pipeline, and 2 of the 3 crash points are after the point where the pipeline stops knowing anything.

</details>
